sections.kicker: Prepared for The Bounce Theory by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: The Bounce Theory has a look of its own. The page does not say so.
sections.keep: The white bounce castle with peach and mauve balloons. No other rental in Southern California looks like it.

pins.quote: Here comes the party everyone will talk about...
pins.what: The headline promises a party. It does not say what kind.
pins.why: Any rental company can promise a party people will talk about. Only you have the white castle and the soft balloons.
pins.how: Name the world you build: all white, soft colours, styled down to the balloons.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: You are compared with every rental in the county on price and availability, not on taste.

pins.area: The logo sits on a pale pink square that does not match the page background
pins.what: The logo sits on its own pale pink square, a slightly different shade from the page.
pins.why: Your best asset looks pasted on instead of part of the page.
pins.how: Supply the logo on a transparent background so it sits on the page the way it sits on a shirt.
pins.label: Your logo
pins.cost: The first thing a visitor sees looks unfinished.

pins.area: The lavender bar and the bright blue pill sit above soft peach and white photography
pins.what: The photo is white, peach and mauve. The bar above it is lavender, the headline is hot coral and the pill is bright blue.
pins.why: The photo shows a softer brand than the page around it. People remember the photo.
pins.how: Take your colours from the photo and let the page fall quiet around it.
pins.label: Your colours
pins.cost: The palette people remember is not the one the site uses.
